anti_overlap: Do not cover Rust-specific crate graph and semver concerns in depth — those belong in a Rust-specialist review; this agent focuses on the PRD-layer extraction strategy framing
Do not cover whether F1's feature decomposition is at the right grain relative to F2/F3/F4 — that belongs to fd-pm-decomposition-discipline
Do not cover whether F1's acceptance criteria are measurable and closeable — that belongs to fd-acceptance-criteria-precision
decision_lens: Engine extractions are not refactors — they are contract negotiations. The moment a codebase is extracted into a dependency, every interface becomes a promise, and the reference implementation loses its authority to change unilaterally. The freeze-protocol question is not administrative overhead: it is the mechanism that prevents the reference implementation from silently invalidating the contract during the migration period. A PRD that gates an engine extraction must specify this protocol or the extraction will drift the moment the first post-PRD change lands in shadow-work.
focus: Whether F1's extraction shape decision is correctly framed as a PRD feature, the freeze-protocol requirement, the workspace-vs-published-crate decision pattern, and the failure modes specific to PRDs that gate library or engine extractions
name: fd-engine-extraction-strategy
persona: Apply the perspective of a library maintainer who has managed the transition of a working embedded codebase into a published library dependency, negotiated the reference-implementation-as-spec problem with multiple downstream consumers, and debugged the specific failure mode where the reference implementation evolves in a direction that breaks the contract the library was supposed to guarantee.
review_areas: F1 requires the extraction shape decision to be recorded in a decision document, but the PRD does not specify who must sign off on the decision. An extraction shape choice has downstream consequences for shadow-work's build system, CI pipeline, and dependency management. If the decision is made unilaterally by the Palettice maintainer without shadow-work's maintainer confirming the topology works for shadow-work's CI, the chosen shape may be correct in principle but unworkable in practice. The PRD should name the signatories for F1's decision document.

The freeze-protocol criterion in F1 requires specifying 'how shadow-work's AgentPersonality changes propagate to Palettice during the migration (auto? proposal? requires Palettice-maintainer signoff?).' But this framing puts propagation in one direction only — from shadow-work to Palettice. During a migration where Palettice is the extraction target, changes also flow in the other direction: Palettice adds new types or changes existing API surface, and shadow-work must adopt them. The freeze protocol as written does not address Palettice-initiated changes during the migration window, which is the more common source of mid-migration drift in practice.

F1's out-of-scope statement says 'whichever interim shape is chosen, A is the eventual destination; this PRD only locks the interim and the trigger.' But the decision document's acceptance criteria do not require the trigger to be operationally specified. 'Promote workspace → published crate when Culture game starts' is a milestone-gated trigger, but 'Culture game starts' is not defined as an observable condition. If F1's decision document records a vague trigger, the shape-A promotion decision will resurface as a negotiation when the time comes, undermining F1's stated goal of settling the question.

The reference-implementation-as-spec failure mode is well-understood in library extraction: the reference implementation is treated as the spec during migration, then evolves post-migration in a direction the library's API cannot accommodate, requiring either a breaking API change or a fork. F1's freeze protocol criterion partially addresses this for shadow-work→Palettice direction. It does not address what happens after the migration closes — specifically, when shadow-work evolves a new personality behaviour that Palettice's API cannot represent. The PRD should flag whether F1's freeze protocol is migration-duration only or permanent.

The PRD notes that 'a trivial end-to-end build verifies the chosen topology.' In a library extraction PRD, 'trivial end-to-end' is load-bearing language: the topology test should cover not just cargo check (type-checking) but cargo test (behaviour). A topology that passes cargo check but breaks cargo test for shadow-work's existing suite has the same problem as a topology that doesn't compile — it does not actually verify that shadow-work can consume Palettice. The criterion should either specify cargo test or explicitly defer shadow-work test coverage to the migration epic with a stated reason.

severity_examples.condition: If Palettice adds a new required field to SoulEvent during the migration window and shadow-work's codebase must adopt it, there is no stated protocol for how that propagation is reviewed or timed. Mid-migration API changes in the extraction target are a known cause of migration stalls — the protocol should be bidirectional.
severity_examples.scenario: Freeze protocol addresses only shadow-work→Palettice direction

severity_examples.condition: A topology that satisfies cargo check --workspace may still fail shadow-work's existing test suite if type-compatible but semantically incompatible types are introduced (e.g., Palettice's SoulEvent and shadow-work's internal event type share a name but differ in fields). The migration epic should not open against a topology that has not been verified to not break shadow-work's tests.
severity_examples.scenario: Topology verified only by cargo check, not cargo test

severity_examples.condition: If F1's decision document records 'promote to published crate when Culture game starts' and 'Culture game starts' has no operational definition, the shape-A promotion decision will be re-litigated at an undefined future time. The trigger should either be a specific observable (a named game feature ships, a named milestone closes) or explicitly deferred with a note that it will be revisited.
severity_examples.scenario: Shape-A promotion trigger is milestone-gated with undefined milestone

success_hints: Check whether the freeze protocol is bidirectional — does it cover Palettice-initiated API changes during the migration window, not only shadow-work-originated changes
Verify the topology acceptance criterion against the three named extraction shapes: is the criterion satisfiable for shape C (two separate repos) or does it assume a workspace topology
Check whether the decision document's required fields include a named signatory from shadow-work's maintainer side, not just Palettice's
Flag any trigger condition for the shape-A promotion that is milestone-gated without a defined milestone observable
task_context: The document's F1 feature gates the migration epic on selecting an extraction shape for shadow-work's consumption of Palettice and specifying a freeze protocol for the migration window. This review focuses on whether F1 is correctly framed as a library-extraction-specific decision — the freeze protocol's completeness, the topology verification criterion's adequacy, and the failure modes specific to reference-implementation-as-spec extractions.
